neighbors.establishing_passage: A carefully designed preprocessing pipeline including deep-learning-based skull stripping and custom intensity windowing is beneficial for accurate segmentation.
Developed an automated method to measure the gray-white matter ratio (GWR) from brain CT scans of patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, assessing prediction of early neurological outcome.
Optimizes NCCT acute-infarct segmentation networks using simulated lesions — synthetic hypoattenuating lesions inserted into brain CT.

1,704 acute stroke patients with admission NCCT; automated chronic lesion segmentation feeding SVM models predicting mRS (AUROC ~0.76-0.77); purely prognostic, no lesion removal or model-intervention test.

Old infarcts, atrophy and leukoaraiosis on baseline CT combined into a brain frailty score (0-3); independently associated with unfavorable mRS shift at day 90, interpreted as vulnerability to ischaemia.
MedEdit conditionally edits prior scans to generate counterfactual stroke scans; the counterfactual-diffusion line adds/removes lesions for what-if synthesis or lesion localization.

A deep CNN (AUC 0.88) predicts final imaging outcome from acute MRI; a second network trained on non-tPA patients is used to assess treatment effect by comparing predicted outcomes under treated vs untreated regimes.
Simulated treatment effects computed by comparing NIHSS predicted under observed reperfusion status with predictions under a counterfactual unsuccessful-reperfusion scenario.

1,000 geometric models built by artificially modifying stenosis location, severity, and length to simulate pre- and postoperative states; a point-cloud network predicts velocity/pressure fields matching CFD.
An ML of tortuosity descriptors and diameter features extracted from MRA data showed a modest correlation between real age and ML-predicted age (best r = 0.532).

Morphological features, including increased tortuosity and reduced vessel diameter, showed strong associations with complications; morphology-informed models outperformed baseline-clinical models (AUROC 0.81 vs 0.73 for early neurological deterioration).
A DL model screens vascular aging from retinal fundus images; features such as vessel calibre, bifurcation, tortuosity may reflect systemic cardiovascular health and future risk.
Medical images contain anatomical priors such as shape, position and topology; incorporating anatomical priors into deep learning has been demonstrated effective for accurate segmentation.
MBGS-UNet with boundary-aware graph attention and uncertainty-gated fusion on ISLES-2022; high-uncertainty responses are mainly distributed near lesion boundaries, where most visible errors occur.

MANCE: interventions should be constrained to the estimated natural representation manifold and better preserve other information during nonlinear concept erasure; LEACE/INLP target linearly decodable concept information.

EPPINN places a Normal-Inverse-Gamma distribution over the physics residual r(t,x) to characterize aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in physics consistency, and enforces the Central Volume Principle by construction by deriving CBF = CBV/(MTT+eps); evaluated on phantoms, ISLES 2018, and clinical cohorts.

CTP maps were significantly different among commercial software even when using identical source data because of differences in tracer-delay sensitivity; delay-sensitive deconvolution overestimates penumbra and final infarct volume.
An efficient early fusion structure was designed to fuse the features of native CTP, CBF, CBV, MTT and Tmax for accurate ischemic stroke prediction.

Higuchi-method fractal dimension applied to voxel-wise CTP time series in phantoms and 149 CTP cases from the public ISLES 2024 dataset; FD correlated with true CBF (rho > 0.9 in phantoms), differentiated core/penumbra/normal (p < 0.001), AUC 0.732 penumbra-vs-normal; no deep learning or trained models were used. Authors Ichikawa, Kondo, Yokoyama (card's 'Lim et al.' is a misattribution).

Modular UNet separating temporal feature extraction from tissue outcome prediction; raw source concentration-time curves (Dice 0.296) matched or beat deconvolved inputs; learned features only correlated (Spearman) against CBF/CBV/MTT/Tmax. Authors Winder et al. (card's 'Robben et al.' is a misattribution).

144 stroke patients; GLMs using a cuboid receptive field of surrounding-tissue pCT information improved final-infarct prediction (AUC 0.89 vs 0.79 without receptive field). First author Klug (card's 'van Os' is a misattribution).

There can be perfusion measurement errors associated with bolus delay/dispersion; methods to account for delay-related errors exist, but dispersion is more difficult and usually left uncorrected; the 2012 follow-up found delay and dispersion information important for accurate infarct prediction in classical predictor models.

The optimal collateral threshold was delay time >6 s (sensitivity 88%, specificity 92%); the CTP collateral index, defined by the ratio of delay time >6 s / delay time >2 s volume, correlated with dynamic CTA collateral scores in 156 patients.

The best model (CTC-Causal) used a causal temporal network with non-deconvolved CTP concentration-time curve data; full text contains no perturbation analyses, counterfactual experiments, or deliberate manipulations of input time-attenuation curves.
